Subject: SLA & Premium Support SKU discussion

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to deciding on a provider for inference serving and Redwood is a leading contender. Before we move to procurement, procurement has asked for two things: a clear breakdown of the premium support SKUs (response windows, escalation routing, on-call coverage) and the associated discount bands for a 12-month commit at our projected usage (~$450k ARR).

Specifically, can you confirm:
- Uptime tiers and corresponding service credits
- Response times for Priority 1 / Priority 2 / Priority 3 incidents
- Escalation coverage (24/7 on-call included? included in which SKU?)
- Any available volume discount beyond the public rate (we're evaluating 10–25% range)

If you can send a one-pager + line-item sheet we can circulate with legal/procurement.

Appreciate it,

Jesse Park
Head of Platform Ops, Olive Systems
jesse@olivesystems.com

Jesse,

Thanks — welcome news. I've attached a compact SLA sheet that maps our uptime bands to service-crediting, response windows, and escalation tiers. High level:
- Standard: 99.5% uptime, business-hours triage, 24/7 monitoring, no included on-call escalation (fast-path for incident remediation via support portal).
- Premium: 99.9% uptime, P1 response target = 1 hour, 24/7 on-call escalation to a named engineer, quarterly operational reviews.
- Platinum: 99.95% uptime, P1 response target = 30 minutes, dedicated escalation leads, 24/7 on-call with guaranteed paging and monthly runbook reviews.

For a 12-month commit at your volume, we typically offer a committed-discount band between 12–20% depending on which SKU you pick and whether you take a Dedicated capacity add-on. I attached our Redwood_SLA_Sheet_v2.xlsx with line items and a sample credit matrix.

Would you be open to a short call Monday to walk procurement through the line items? If you want a faster path, we can propose a single combined SKU with a 15% discount and a DocuSign link today.

Quick asks:
- Can we do 15% off for Premium (99.9%) with Dedicated burst option w/ a 3-month true-up?
- If not, what delta to hit 20%? where does on-call coverage/engineer assignment get pricey?

Notes: procurement cares about a single line item they can sign fast. They prefer a one-page SLA + DocuSign. CCing Vanessa for final approvals path.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA & Premium Support SKU discussion

Michael —

I ran numbers. Short answer: 15% is workable if we keep Olive on Premium (99.9%) without a dedicated named-engineer SLA (we can include 24/7 escalation but no dedicated engineer assignment). That preserves margin and keeps operational risk manageable. Details:
- Premium (no named engineer): 15% off list, includes P1 = 1h, P2 = 4h, P3 = 24h; 24/7 escalation routing, quarterly reviews; crediting as per sheet (max 10% annual credit).
- Premium + Named Engineer (Platinum-ish): 20% off if they commit to Dedicated capacity + 12-month minimum MRC equal to their projected ARR/12 (effectively one year pre-commit). Named-engineer adds ~7–9% cost to our OPEX assumption, so that's why we need the deeper discount.
- If they want a single-line SKU for procurement we can package Premium + burst Dedicated as a single product code with a footnote for true-up. That keeps legal simple.

I've attached a two-column pricing_notes.pdf that lays out margin sensitivity and recommended counters.

—Laura
Director, Commercial Pricing
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA & Premium Support SKU discussion

Adding margin-preserving alternative:
- Offer 15% off Premium with a performance collar: if measured uptime for any quarter falls below 99.85%, we apply a one-time supplementary credit (0.5% of monthly invoice for that month), capped at cumulative 5% for the year. This reduces payout tail-risk vs the standard credit matrix while being attractive to procurement.
- For named-engineer requests, consider a blended 18% discount if Olive agrees to a fixed on-call rotation contribution fee (pass-through) to offset cost.

If Laura is comfortable with the numbers, I'm fine with 15% on Premium and 18% blended for named engineer contingent on Dedicated.

—Ben
Head of Renewals & Packaging
ben_carter@redwood.com

Jesse — thanks for the patience while we pulled this together. Final proposal summary below (packaged for procurement):

Proposal (single-line SKU for signature):
- SKU: Redwood Premium + Burst Dedicated (single procurement line)
- Uptime: 99.9% target; P1 response = 1 hour, P2 = 4 hours, P3 = 24 hours
- Escalation: 24/7 escalation routing included; named engineer assignment is optional add-on
- Credits: standard credit matrix (see attachment) with a performance collar: quarterly below 99.85% triggers supplementary credit (0.5% monthly invoice for the affected month), annual cap 5%
- Pricing: 15% off list for Premium packaged SKU; 18% blended if Olive accepts named-engineer add-on and Dedicated capacity commitment (12 months, true-up allowed)

Next steps:
1) If the 15% / single-line SKU looks good I can send a DocuSign today (link below) and legal can take the standard SLA attachment we've included.
2) If procurement wants the named engineer we will need a brief call to align on scope and on-call rotation before finalizing the 18% blended rate.
